en: The Śrī Dakṣiṇāmūrti Stotra
May that abode, which is to be venerated by the lay disciples and where [the Lord] took up residence at the foot of the banyan tree—
may that abode, in the form of consciousness, awaken in my mind through its own embodiment endowed with compassion.
I beheld the primordial Teacher, a treasury of undiminished mercy, at the base of the banyan tree.

With silence adorned by a gentle smile, he dispels the darkness of the world of great sages; with a particular mudrā that has driven away the entire host of darkness, the Great God repeatedly casts aside the illusion of the sages through his compassion and bestows the realization: "Thou art That."
I bow to the Guru of gurus, who gazes with side-long glances that are waves of the nectar of boundless compassion upon the sages scorched by the heat of this harsh saṃsāra. Today,
by his extraordinary grace, the Lord dwelling at the foot of the banyan tree has manifested his presence before me.
May he who, having taught the Vidyā whose form is the syllable Oṃ, dispels the darkness of ignorance.

I behold the Teacher, immeasurable, the dawn for the blindness of beginningless ignorance— he whose limbs are fashioned like the digits of the moon, and whose form is bound as if with strings of pearls.
I bow to the Lord who is possessed of meditative concentration, whose left foot rests upon his own right knee, whose yogic cloth (yogapaṭṭa) adorns his feet and belly,
and who has placed his foot upon the body of Apasmṛti (the personification of forgetfulness).
Though he is but a youth, he is capable of instructing the sages who dwell with him regarding the true meaning of reality.

I bow to that Teacher, who is the abode of wondrous qualities, brought forth by the nets of merit from former lives. (8) May the Teacher-Crest-Jewel appear before me, holding an axe as a mudrā in one hand and a deer in the other, with his hands resting upon his own knees. (9)
I behold a certain lord of teachers, who is anointed with the ashes of the body of Love, clad in a tiger-skin garment,
and who is a submarine fire to the ocean of ignorance.
He possesses a beautiful smile, wears the crescent moon as his crest-jewel, holds a lute, and has a clearly manifest mass of matted locks.
Some yogins worship you, who take delight in the experience of the internal resonance (nāda) they have acquired;

we worship that Great Lord in the form of Dakṣiṇāmūrti, whom sages such as Śuka and others— free from desires and permeated by selflessness— worship for the sake of pacifying the great agony of delusion.

May that Lord—who, with a beauty surpassing the jasmine and the kandalī flower, dwells at the foot of the banyan tree; who honors the assembly of sages with glances that are like the waters of the nectar of compassion;
and who dispels the darkness of delusion through such awakening—enlighten me with his hand bearing the *mudrā*, saying "That art Thou.
[May he do so] together with those whose limbs are not pale, whose eyes are not on the forehead, whose dress is not unpeaceful, and who are not adorned with serpents.
Enough for us of these immortals, whose sleep has been cast off by the seal of awakening and whose desires are fulfilled.
How many deities exist on this earth? In my mind, they do not even exist.
The deity who is inclined toward the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) alone is capable of bestowing grace upon those of dull intellect.
To him who is joyful, who wears the charming crescent moon as an ornament, and whose form is made beautiful by the smearing of ashes—to him [I bow].
Salutations to the Great Splendor who dwells at the foot of the banyan tree, who is most skillful in creating the illusory web of the universe.

(16) With matted locks hanging down on all sides, with a crescent moon—the sole remnant of its digits—upon your head, and with a moon-like face whose forehead is visible, you shine within the minds of those who are pure. (17)
O Consort of Umā, you manifest the state of the full moon for your lay devotees;
for today, by the mere sight of you, my mind—like a moonstone—melts away with joy. 18. He who, with delight, contemplates your gracious form, which bears the charming crescent moon upon its crest—
One obtains sovereignty, long life, and knowledge, and finally the great secret of Vedānta.
Thus ends the *Dakṣiṇāmūrtistotra* composed by the venerable Śaṅkarabhāratī Svāmin.
